subject: physics_2
question_text: Explain parallel combination of capacitors. Derive the formula for equivalent capacitance.

verification.note: The 1+2+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two structural checks are IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the two-book union check (the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only) and the past-paper back-test (the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers). Hand-checked: in parallel V is common, Q = Q₁+Q₂+Q₃ with Qᵢ = CᵢV gives C = C₁+C₂+C₃ — the book's chain, correct (its 'cahrge' typo not copied).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The arrangement
lines: In parallel, the first plates of all the
capacitors join one common terminal and the
second plates join the other. The two common
Each capacitor has the full applied V; the
steps.margin_note: First mark. Common terminals; same V on each, charge divides.
steps.why: Joined to the same two terminals, every capacitor reads the same potential difference — so here it is the CHARGE that splits, the mirror image of the series case.
common_mistakes: Saying the charge is the same on each — in parallel it is V that is common.
Describing plate-to-plate joining — that is the series arrangement.

recall.must_convey: That all first plates join one terminal and all second plates the other, so each capacitor has the full V and the charge divides.
reject: C is C one plus C two plus C three

steps.memory_tip: Parallel: one V for all, the Q splits.

steps.label: The figure
steps.margin_note: Three branches between the same two vertical wires, battery at the bottom.
steps.why: The three branches hang between the same two wires — the picture of why one V reaches every capacitor while the battery's charge has three ways to divide.
common_mistakes: Chaining the capacitors along one wire — that is the series figure.

recall.must_convey: That three capacitors are drawn as three branches between the same two wires with the battery across them.
reject: Q is Q one plus Q two plus Q three

steps.memory_tip: A ladder: two rails, three rungs, each rung a capacitor.

steps.label: Adding the charges
lines: The total charge drawn from the battery is
With the common V across each capacitor,

lines.text: Q₁ = C₁V, Q₂ = C₂V, Q₃ = C₃V

lines: If C is the equivalent capacitance, Q = CV:
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Q adds; each Qᵢ is its own Cᵢ times the same V.
steps.why: The equivalent capacitor is the one that draws the same total Q at the same V — writing Q = CV beside the sum is what turns the arrangement into the formula.
common_mistakes: Adding potential differences instead of charges — the V's are all equal here.
Using different voltages V₁, V₂, V₃ — parallel forces one common V.

recall.must_convey: That the total charge is the sum of the three, each equal to its C times the common V.
accept: Q is Q one plus Q two plus Q three
each Q is C times V

steps.memory_tip: Parallel: the Q's add up, the V factors out.

steps.label: The equivalent capacitance
lines: The equivalent C is larger than the largest
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Box the plain sum and note that C comes out larger.
steps.why: Plates side by side act as one capacitor of combined area, and C grows with area — so parallel capacitances simply add.
common_mistakes: Writing 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + 1/C₃ — that is the series formula.

recall.must_convey: That C equals C one plus C two plus C three, larger than the largest.
accept: C is C one plus C two plus C three
reject: one by C is the sum of one by C i

steps.memory_tip: Parallel plates pool their area — capacitances add straight.

insider_note: The middle marks want Q₁ = C₁V etc. with the SAME V in every term — the mirror of the series card, and the two are the classic mix-up pair.
